level.title: Boarding Crisis
level.tagline: The hospital is full. More doctors will not fix it.
briefing: Simulation five. Thursday and Friday. Every inpatient bed in the hospital is full.
When you admit someone, they stay in one of your beds until a ward bed frees up. Those beds are the only place your doctors can see new patients.

You can call in more doctors. You can open the fast track. You can ask the hospital to declare a full-capacity protocol, which pushes the wards to discharge faster. Choose carefully what the problem really is.

pass: Your department was never short of doctors. It was short of beds, because the hospital behind it was full.
Fixes that route patients around the blocked beds, or get the wards moving, work. Extra doctors mostly stand around waiting for a bed to free up.
fail: Look at who was in your beds: admitted patients with nowhere to go. More staff in the ED cannot empty a ward.
Find a way to treat patients who do not need a main bed, and a way to get the hospital to take its patients.

goals.label: Fewer than 8% leave without being seen
Admitted patients board for under 6 hours on average
